sentences.en: But let's start with a bit of background.

sentences.zh: 我仍然为了不同的目的在使用各种不同的语言。

sentences.en: I'm still using a variety of different languages for different purposes.

sentences.en: But Java is one of the languages I'm trying to forget about.

sentences.en: Oh, that's mixed a lot.

sentences.en: Live there.

sentences.en: I spent half a year in Rome and I decided that I just need to get independent and start earning my own money and live in my own way.
sentences.zh: 所以回来后，我便开始工作了。

sentences.en: So after coming back, I started working.
sentences.zh: 同时修两个专业还要兼顾工作，这可以说是相当疯狂。

sentences.en: And it wasn't full-time initially, but it was enough to survive from.

sentences.en: In the meantime, I was working as a developer.
sentences.zh: 我完成了那两个学位。

sentences.en: I finished those two degrees.

sentences.en: And so my career mixed both of those paths.

sentences.en: What were your degrees?

sentences.zh: 一个是计算机科学。

sentences.en: One was computer science.
sentences.zh: 另一个更偏向于电信方向。

sentences.en: Another one is closer to telecommunication.
sentences.zh: 啊，原来如此，挺酷的。

sentences.en: Ah, okay, cool.

sentences.en: Nevertheless, the story with Kotlin has started for me when I worked as an Android.
sentences.zh: 我是 Kotlin 的早期采用者之一。

sentences.en: developer and I was one of the early adapters of Kotlin.
sentences.zh: 当年的社区氛围——你知道的，虽然现在的社区氛围依然很好，但当年和现在完全无法比拟。

sentences.en: And back then, the community was, you know, I mean, community is still very positive, but it's absolutely incomparable what was then and what is now.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们的社区发展得太大了，以至于你根本无法认识所有人。

sentences.en: You know, our community grew so much that no one, I mean, you cannot know all those people.
sentences.zh: 字面意思上，有数以百万计的人在用 Kotlin。

sentences.en: There are literally millions of people using Kotlin.
sentences.zh: 而在当时，那是一个非常小众的弄潮儿社区，我们都充满热情，互相支持。

sentences.en: Back then, it was a very small hipster community where we all were passionate and we were all supporting each other.
sentences.zh: 那段时光真的非常有意思。

sentences.en: And it was so, so fun.
sentences.zh: 我当时就只想尽可能多地做些贡献。

sentences.en: And I just wanted to give as much as I could.
sentences.zh: 我写关于 Kotlin 的文章，做关于 Kotlin 的演讲，我真的对推广它充满了热情。

sentences.en: And I was writing about Kotlin and speaking about Kotlin and I was truly passionate about promoting it.
sentences.zh: 我至今仍然热衷于教授 Kotlin 和编程，但你知道，感觉已经不完全一样了。

sentences.en: I still am in teaching Kotlin and teaching programming in general, but, you know, that's not the same.
sentences.zh: 昨天我去徒步了很久。

sentences.en: Yeah, I did a lot of hiking yesterday.
sentences.zh: 不知怎么的，让我想起了一个比方：如果你在走一条非常大众的徒步路线，

sentences.en: And so, for some reason, metaphor kind of comes to mind where, you know, if you're hiking this trail that's really common,
sentences.zh: 也许它铺好了路或者别的什么，那么你完全可以自己一个人去爬。

sentences.en: maybe it's paved or something like that, then you can really hike it by yourself.
sentences.zh: 但如果你开始深入荒野，那么当遇到麻烦时，你往往需要一种能联系到别人的途径，对吧？

sentences.en: But if you start going out in the wilderness, then you kind of need a way to reach somebody if something goes wrong, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，一开始当你用 Kotlin 开发安卓时，你就像是身处荒野之中。

sentences.en: And so, in the beginning, when you're writing Kotlin for Android, you're kind of out there.
sentences.zh: 因此你需要一根救命稻草，特别是如果你用它来工作而且它必须正常运行，这可不仅仅是个爱好。

sentences.en: And so, you need a lifeline, especially, you know, if you're doing it for work and it has to work, it's not just a hobby.
sentences.zh: 这时候你就需要一个社区。

sentences.en: Then you need a community.
sentences.zh: 你需要一个能够求助的对象，一个真正的超级专家。

sentences.en: You need somebody that you can go to who is, you know, uber expert.
sentences.zh: 然后你可以对他说：“听着，我遇到了这个非常晦涩难懂的错误。”

sentences.en: And you can say, look, I'm getting this, you know, really esoteric error.
sentences.zh: “请帮帮我。”

sentences.en: Please help me.
sentences.zh: 而现在，这条路可能已经被踩得太熟了，以至于你根本不需要进行太多社交就能完成你的应用。

sentences.en: And now, maybe the path is just so well-traveled that you don't have to really socialize to get your app done.
sentences.zh: 所以，这可以说是福祸相依吧。

sentences.en: So, it's just, you know, a blessing and a curse at the same time.
sentences.zh: 是的，这确实改变了很多。

sentences.en: Yes, and that does change a lot.
sentences.zh: 我还记得当年谷歌宣布 Kotlin 成为……

sentences.en: I remember when Google announced that Kotlin is becoming the...
sentences.zh: 当时，它是安卓的另一种可选语言。

sentences.en: Back then, it was another language for Android.
sentences.zh: 而现在，它是安卓开发的首选语言。

sentences.en: Right now, it's the primary language for Android development.
sentences.zh: 但我依然记得他们宣布 Kotlin 继 Java 之后成为安卓开发又一门语言的那一天。

sentences.en: But I remember the day when they announced that it's becoming another language for Android development after Java.
sentences.zh: 我当时想：“太好了，我们要开香槟庆祝。”

sentences.en: And I was like, okay, we are opening Champaign.
sentences.zh: 对我们来说这是个重大的日子。

sentences.en: It's a huge day for us.
sentences.zh: 而我的一位朋友，他年纪稍大一些，在编程社区待的时间更久，他当时却显得很难过。

sentences.en: And a friend of mine who was a bit older, for a bit longer in this programming community, he was really sad.
sentences.zh: 他看着我说：“我们不再是弄潮儿了，一切都要变了。”

sentences.en: And he just looked at me and he said, we just stopped being hipsters and everything changes now.
sentences.zh: 我记得大概一年后，他就放弃了 Kotlin，转去搞另一个大项目了。

sentences.en: And I believe like a year later, he left Kotlin and he started another big thing.
sentences.zh: 哦？那是什么大项目？

sentences.en: Oh, what is this big thing?
sentences.zh: 他的下一个大项目是什么？

sentences.en: What is his next big thing?
sentences.zh: 他一头扎进了 Aeternum 和那些智能合约领域。

sentences.en: He got into Aeternum and all those smart contracts.
sentences.zh: 哦，原来如此。

sentences.en: Oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 我不太确定这后来是不是真的成了一个大火的项目，我也从没有真正去深入研究过。

sentences.en: I'm not sure if this truly became a big thing, but I've never truly researched that.
sentences.zh: 但他刚开始做的时候显得非常着迷。

sentences.en: But he was very fascinated when he started that.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 真是个创新者。

sentences.en: What an innovator.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，确实。

sentences.en: I mean, yeah.
sentences.zh: 其实我对智能合约也不是很了解，但到现在这几乎成了一个家喻户晓的词汇。

sentences.en: I mean, I don't know very much about smart contracts either, but it's almost a household name at this point.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有许多像他这样的人。

sentences.en: I mean, there are many people like that.
sentences.zh: 我有幸在相当多的初创公司工作过。

sentences.en: I had a pleasure to work in quite a few startups.
sentences.zh: 我真正享受的一点是人们的心态，大家只想致力于改变现状的事情，去改变世界，做出非常非常了不起的成就。

sentences.en: And one thing that I truly enjoyed is the mindset of people, that people just want to work on the break changing things and change the world and do amazing, amazing things.
sentences.zh: 而其中许多人在初创公司最终成长为一家成熟的公司时，本可以在那里留下来赚大钱，

sentences.en: And many of those people, when startup finally becomes a serious company, many of those people can stay there and make great money,
sentences.zh: 但他们却选择离开，去投入到另一个大项目中。

sentences.en: but they decide to leave it instead to work on another big thing.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 所以，好吧，当时你即将大学毕业，在构建安卓应用，编写大量的 Java 代码，并且痛恨这种生活。

sentences.en: So, okay, so you were finishing up university and you're building Android, you're working on Android apps and writing a lot of Java and hating life.
sentences.zh: 你有一个“痛恨生活工厂”，然后还有一个“工厂实现工厂”。

sentences.en: And you had a life-hating factory and then a factory implementation factory.
sentences.zh: 你当时就在想：“天哪，为什么我会有上百万个不同的工厂？”

sentences.en: And you're just, oh, my God, why do I have a million different factories?
sentences.zh: 而且每个回调函数都必须是一个类。

sentences.en: And like every callback has to be a class.
sentences.zh: 这简直把所有人都逼疯了，对吧？

sentences.en: And so it's just driving everyone crazy, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，也许你可以聊聊——我刚才用了一些刻板印象——但究竟有哪些事情是真正让你对 Java 感到厌烦的？

sentences.en: So, well, maybe you could talk about, you know, I threw out some stereotypes there, but what are the things specifically that really bothered you about Java?
sentences.zh: 我认为最基础形态的 Kotlin 其实并没有什么真正崭新的东西。

sentences.en: I think that the Kotlin in its most basic form is nothing really new.
sentences.zh: 现在当然有一些新特性，比如协程或多平台能力，这些确实很强大，对吧？

sentences.en: There are new things right now, like coroutines or multi-platform capabilities, and they are big, okay?
sentences.zh: 但 Kotlin 的基石，在我看来，就是 Java 本该有的样子。

sentences.en: But the base of Kotlin is just, I believe, how Java should look like.
sentences.zh: 如果 Java 当初能够做出艰难的决定并按照应有的方式不断演进，它大致就会长成这个样子。

sentences.en: It is how I think Java would look like, more or less, if it were making hard decisions and evolving as it should evolve.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，当然，Java 的大问题在于向后兼容性。

sentences.en: You know, of course, the big problem of Java is backward compatibility.
sentences.zh: 为了不破坏人们的代码，他们不轻易改变。

sentences.en: They do not change to not break people's code.
sentences.zh: 所以我并不是说 Java 做出了糟糕的决定。

sentences.en: So I'm not saying that Java made a poor decision.
sentences.zh: 我只是说，如果 Java 能够做出它本该做出的改变，依我之见，它最终看起来就会很像现在的 Kotlin。

sentences.en: I'm just saying that if Java would make the changes it should make, in my opinion, it would end up looking something like Kotlin looks like right now.
sentences.zh: 再加上它从一开始就设计好的一些优秀特性。

sentences.en: Plus, it has some things that were designed well from the beginning.
sentences.zh: 所以 Kotlin 拥有一个组织得非常出色的类型系统，这是很多人觉得不重要，但从我们编写代码的角度来看却极其极其重要的东西。

sentences.en: So Kotlin has a really well-organized typing system, something people do not see as important, but it's extremely, extremely important from the perspective of using our code.
sentences.zh: 所以当你提到组织良好的类型系统时，是指类型提示和类型推断吗？

sentences.en: So when you say organized type system, are you talking about the type hints and the type inference?
sentences.zh: 也就是说你可以直接写类似 `val x = 3` 的代码，而不必去纠结它究竟是 int 还是 long，或者处理一堆这方面的事情？

sentences.en: So you could say, you know, val x equals 3, and you don't have to go and find out, is it an int or a long, or deal with a lot of that?
sentences.zh: 还是说究竟是什么让它变得井然有序？

sentences.en: Or what makes it organized?
sentences.zh: 举个例子，在 Kotlin 中，从一开始你就有专门的类型来表示可空类型和不可空类型。

sentences.en: So, for instance, in Kotlin, from the beginning, you have a type to represent nullable and not nullable types.
sentences.zh: 啊，对的。

sentences.en: Ah, right.
sentences.zh: 这极其重要，因为只有这样，你才能拥有恰当的类型安全机制，而这依然是大多数现代语言尚未完美实现的功能。

sentences.en: What is extremely important, because only then you can have proper type safety mechanisms, something that is still not very well implemented by most modern languages.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，Kotlin 在这些类型之间建立了一种非常严格的层级关系。

sentences.en: And what is more, Kotlin made a very strict relationship between those types.
sentences.zh: 因此，可空类型是不可空类型的超类型，这就为许多重要的应用场景打开了大门。

sentences.en: So a nullable type is a super type of not nullable type, what opens a door for many important use cases.
sentences.zh: 在 Kotlin 中，一切皆为表达式。

sentences.en: In Kotlin, everything is an expression.
sentences.zh: 我们还有 Nothing 类型，即空类型，它是所有类型的子类型，但没有任何实例。

sentences.en: We also have a nothing type, an empty type, that is a subtype of all the type, but has no instances.
sentences.zh: 对于不使用它的人来说，这也是一个看似微不足道的细节。

sentences.en: It's another thing that seems minor from people who do not use that.
sentences.zh: 但在某些使用场景中，它真的极其重要，能够让语言表现得非常完美。

sentences.en: But it's really, really important on some use cases that allows language to truly behave well.
sentences.zh: 这些都是小地方，一旦一门语言发布之后，这些东西是极难修复的，但在 Kotlin 中，从一开始就把这些做得非常非常好。

sentences.en: Those are small things that are very hard to repair in the language once you publish that, but that were done really, really well in Kotlin from the beginning.
sentences.zh: 太酷了。

sentences.en: Cool.
sentences.zh: 对，这说得通。

sentences.en: Yeah, that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 那么在底层究竟会发生什么，Kotlin 是一门 JVM 语言吗？

sentences.en: What actually happens under the hood when you, is Kotlin a JVM language?
sentences.zh: 它是被编译到 JVM，还是完全不同的东西？

sentences.en: So does Kotlin compile down to the JVM, or is it something different entirely?
sentences.zh: 总的来说，Kotlin 是一门编译型语言。

sentences.en: In general, Kotlin is a compiled language.
sentences.zh: 所以它会被编译成更简单的形式。

sentences.en: So it is compiled to something more simple.
sentences.zh: 在最常使用的版本中，它就像 Java 一样，会被编译成 JVM 字节码。

sentences.en: And in the version that is most often used, it is compiled into JVM bytecode, just like Java.
sentences.zh: 然而，Kotlin 有不同的变体，或者你可以称之为平台目标。

sentences.en: However, there are different flavors of Kotlin, or you can say platform targets.
sentences.zh: 比如有被编译成 JavaScript 的 Kotlin JS。

sentences.en: There is a Kotlin JS that is compiled into JavaScript.
sentences.zh: 还有被编译成本地代码的 Kotlin Native。

sentences.en: And there is Kotlin Native that is compiled into the native code.
sentences.zh: 为什么这很重要？

sentences.en: Why is it important?
sentences.zh: 在安卓开发中，这很关键，因为它允许我们编写能够同时在安卓和 iOS 上运行的库。

sentences.en: On Android, it is important because it allows us to make libraries that are used both by Android and by iOS.
sentences.zh: 这样我们就能轻松实现共享的公共部分。

sentences.en: So we can easily make a common part.
sentences.zh: 团队也非常乐意把越来越多的逻辑放到这些公共部分中去。

sentences.en: And teams like to include more and more on those common parts.
sentences.zh: 业务逻辑，你知道的，这两个平台通常都是一样的。

sentences.en: Business logic, you know, this is generally the same for both platforMs.
sentences.zh: 甚至连视图也是如此，现在有一种新方法，

sentences.en: Even views, there is this new approach,
sentences.zh: 那就是 Jetpack Compose 库，它允许你使用纯 Kotlin，通过 Kotlin DSL 以非常精美的风格来创建视图，并且享有优秀的自动补全和绝对的类型安全。

sentences.en: the Jetpack Compose library that allows you to create views in a pure Kotlin using a Kotlin DSL in a really nice style with a nice autocompletion and with absolute type safety.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，Jetpack Compose 项目可以被编译到 JVM，从而在安卓或桌面上运行。

sentences.en: And, you know, projects in Jetpack Compose can be compiled to JVM and run on Android or on desktop.
sentences.zh: 但它们也可以被编译成 JS 作为网页展示，或者被编译成本地代码，成为你想要的任何系统的原生应用。

sentences.en: But they can be also compiled into JS and be displayed as a website or be compiled into a native code and be a native application for whatever system you want.
sentences.zh: 结束

sentences.en: So that's a new thing and very, very powerful that comes from the fact that Kotlin is a multi-platform language.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个新特性，而且非常非常强大，这源于Kotlin是一门多平台语言的事实。

sentences.en: You can use Kotlin to write on any of those platforms or you can use it to write a module that can be compiled into multiple platforms at the same time.
sentences.zh: 你可以使用Kotlin在其中任何一个平台上进行开发，也可以用它来编写一个能同时编译到多个平台的模块。

sentences.en: How does the iOS work?
sentences.zh: iOS是怎么运作的呢？

sentences.en: So you would compile to like a native library?
sentences.zh: 所以你会把它编译成类似于原生库的东西吗？

sentences.en: You'd have to somehow create some kind of Objective-C Interop or something, right?
sentences.zh: 你得想办法创建某种Objective-C的互操作层之类的东西，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: So you could say that the result code is the same and that's what you would have if you would compile an Objective-C.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以说生成的结果代码是一样的，这就跟你编译Objective-C时得到的一样。

sentences.en: And yes, Objective-C is used here to Interop with Swift or with Objective-C Project.
sentences.zh: 是的，这里使用Objective-C是为了与Swift或Objective-C项目进行互操作。

sentences.en: Oh, interesting.
sentences.zh: 哦，有意思。

sentences.en: Very cool.
sentences.zh: 太酷了。

sentences.en: Does it generate the Interop layer for you or do you have to write that yourself?
sentences.zh: 它是为你生成互操作层，还是必须自己编写？

sentences.en: It generates it.
sentences.zh: 它会自动生成。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇。

sentences.en: That's super cool.
sentences.zh: 这太酷了。

sentences.en: For other languages as well.
sentences.zh: 对于其他语言也是如此。

sentences.en: I do not have much experience with this native part.
sentences.zh: 我对这部分原生开发没有太多经验。

sentences.en: However, recently I had the experience, I was writing a library.
sentences.zh: 不过最近我有了这方面的经验，当时我在写一个库。

sentences.en: I'm learning things using a flashcards in a program called Anki.
sentences.zh: 我正在用一个叫做Anki的程序通过闪卡来学习东西。

sentences.en: And I wanted to make notes that are automatically generating notes for this Anki program.
sentences.zh: 我想做一些笔记，能为这个Anki程序自动生成复习卡片。

sentences.en: And I wrote a program for that in Kotlin.
sentences.zh: 为此我用Kotlin写了一个程序。

sentences.en: I default in Kotlin JVM.
sentences.zh: 我的默认环境是Kotlin JVM。

sentences.en: But to transform my notes into Anki or Anki Deck into notes because it goes in both directions, I needed to start a JVM program every time.
sentences.zh: 但为了把我的笔记转换成Anki格式，或者把Anki牌组转换成笔记（因为它是双向的），我每次都得启动一个JVM程序。

sentences.en: I did not like that.
sentences.zh: 我不太喜欢那样。

sentences.en: And then I figured out I'm using the Obsidian note for it's a program for notes, quite a popular one recently, where you write all your notes in Markdown.
sentences.zh: 后来我发现我可以用Obsidian——这是一个做笔记的程序，最近挺受欢迎的，你所有的笔记都是用Markdown写的。

sentences.en: And I figured out that you can make a plugin for Obsidian.
sentences.zh: 我发现你可以为Obsidian制作一个插件。

sentences.en: And if you write a plugin for Obsidian, you can add a button that starts some process, basically.
sentences.zh: 如果你为Obsidian写了一个插件，基本上就可以添加一个按钮来启动某种进程。

sentences.en: And then I migrated this Kotlin code from Java into Kotlin.js and used it to make a plugin for Obsidian from that.
sentences.zh: 然后我把这段Kotlin代码从Java迁移到了Kotlin.js，并用它制作了一个Obsidian插件。

sentences.en: It was very, very easy.
sentences.zh: 过程非常非常简单。

sentences.en: Practically no effort needed.
sentences.zh: 几乎不需要什么工作量。

sentences.en: I think the only thing that I needed to change is that I was using the files API and I just needed to get rid of that.
sentences.zh: 我想我唯一需要修改的地方是我用了文件API，而我只需要去掉它就行了。

sentences.en: And that's it.
sentences.zh: 就这样。

sentences.en: Everything else worked.
sentences.zh: 其他一切都能正常运行。

sentences.en: Exactly the same way.
sentences.zh: 效果完全一样。

sentences.en: And I'm still playing with that, but I do have it working.
sentences.zh: 我还在琢磨它，但它已经能跑通了。

sentences.en: So I now have an Obsidian plugin where I have a button, you know, push to Anki or pull from Anki.
sentences.zh: 所以我现在有了一个Obsidian插件，里面有一个按钮，你知道的，点击就能推送到Anki或从Anki拉取。

sentences.en: And it does work.
sentences.zh: 而且它确实管用。

sentences.en: I'm still working on that until it is stable, until I announce that and publish it.
sentences.zh: 我还在继续完善它，直到它足够稳定，然后我才会宣布并发布它。

sentences.en: But for my own use, it is already usable and it did not take so much time.
sentences.zh: 但对于我自己的使用来说，它已经派上用场了，而且没花太多时间。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's really, really cool.
sentences.zh: 对，这真的非常非常酷。

sentences.en: So, yeah, actually, Obsidian looks awesome.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，其实Obsidian看起来挺棒的。

sentences.en: I just went to obsidian.md and took a look.
sentences.zh: 我刚刚访问了obsidian.md看了一眼。

sentences.en: This is, I use Workflow-y.
sentences.zh: 这个嘛，我用的是Workflow-y。

sentences.en: I'm not crazy about it.
sentences.zh: 我对它并不是那么痴迷。

sentences.en: I'm definitely going to check out Obsidian.
sentences.zh: 我绝对要去看一下Obsidian。

sentences.en: Obsidian.
sentences.zh: Obsidian。

sentences.en: This looks awesome.
sentences.zh: 这看起来太棒了。

sentences.en: But, yeah, this is, you know, as someone, I've only made apps as kind of a hobby.
sentences.zh: 不过，话又说回来，你知道的，作为一个只把做应用当成业余爱好的人。

sentences.en: And so I've never had a strong desire to make an app for iOS and Android.
sentences.zh: 所以我从来没有过那种一定要为iOS和Android开发应用的强烈愿望。

sentences.en: I mean, the same app.
sentences.zh: 我是指同一个应用。

sentences.en: And so I always kind of wondered how people, you know, dealt with that.
sentences.zh: 所以我一直挺好奇大家是怎么处理这事的。

sentences.en: And this seems like a really clever way where you write in Kotlin and now you get a, you know, your business logic in a shared library that then you interact with, you know,
sentences.zh: 这似乎是一个非常巧妙的方法：你用Kotlin编写代码，现在你的业务逻辑就包含在一个共享库里，然后你可以通过……你知道的，

sentences.en: from your main, you know, view code.
sentences.zh: 你的主视图代码去与它交互。

sentences.en: And it's really cool.
sentences.zh: 这真的很酷。

sentences.en: So you were working on apps in Java.
sentences.zh: 所以你以前是用Java开发应用的。

sentences.en: And at some point you either had to convince your company to switch to Kotlin or you had to change jobs.
sentences.zh: 在某个时候，要么你得说服公司转向Kotlin，要么你就得换工作。

sentences.en: So what happened there?
sentences.zh: 那么当时情况是怎样的？

sentences.en: And how did that play out?
sentences.zh: 结果如何呢？

sentences.en: I needed to change job.
sentences.zh: 我不得不换工作。

sentences.en: I mean, back then there was, there were maybe a few companies in Poland using Kotlin and I sent resume to probably all of them.
sentences.zh: 我是说，当时波兰可能只有少数几家公司在用Kotlin，我大概把简历投给了所有这些公司。

sentences.en: And, you know, Kotlin was still in beta back then and no big company wanted to use it.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，那时候Kotlin还在测试阶段，没有大公司愿意用它。

sentences.en: However, startups did use that.
sentences.zh: 不过初创公司确实在用。

sentences.en: So the company that accepted me was a doc planner, probably don't know about it because it's not present in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以录用我的那家公司叫Docplanner，你可能没听说过，因为它在美国没有业务。

sentences.en: It's present in some Europe and a big part of South America.
sentences.zh: 它在欧洲的一些国家以及南美的大部分地区都有业务。

sentences.en: That's a service where as a doctor, you can register and people can rate you.
sentences.zh: 那是一个服务平台，作为医生你可以在上面注册，人们可以对你进行评价。

sentences.en: You can have calendar and it's literally like an assistant for doctors.
sentences.zh: 你可以使用日历，它简直就像是医生的助手。

sentences.en: And patients can, you know, find the best doctors and can check their prices.
sentences.zh: 患者也可以在上面寻找最好的医生，并查看他们的诊疗费用。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's interesting.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这很有意思。

sentences.en: By, you know, being passionate about this early technology and then picking companies that are using it,
sentences.zh: 通过对这种早期技术充满热情，然后选择那些正在使用它的公司，

sentences.en: you're kind of by definition picking companies that are sort of on the cutting edge.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，你就是在选择那些处于前沿领域的公司。

sentences.en: And for them to take a risk, it means that their leadership must be pretty technical.
sentences.zh: 对它们来说，愿意承担风险意味着它们的领导层一定具备很强的技术背景。

sentences.en: It's kind of like, it's really interesting.
sentences.zh: 这感觉挺有意思的。

sentences.en: It's like, I feel like it's a good signal for picking companies to join, right?
sentences.zh: 就好像，我觉得这是挑选要加入的公司的优质信号，对吧？

sentences.en: Is if they have this sort of same passion that you do about some emerging technology, then I think it's a really good way to build alignment.
sentences.zh: 那就是如果他们对某些新兴技术和你有着同样的激情，那么我认为这是建立志同道合关系的好方法。

sentences.en: Yes, I even heard that it's a strategy of some companies that they intentionally use those new and untested technologies.
sentences.zh: 是的，我甚至听说这是某些公司的一种策略，他们故意使用那些崭新且未经检验的技术。

sentences.en: So they find people who are kind of crazy, who are willing to have less money and probably more work for doing what is their passion and what they love to do.
sentences.zh: 这样他们就能找到那些有点疯狂的人，这些人愿意为了做自己热爱的事情而拿更少的薪水、干更多的工作。

sentences.en: Also, it's a good strategy for companies like startups, because it's actually easier to find people.
sentences.zh: 另外，这对于初创公司这样的企业来说也是个好策略，因为实际上这样更容易招到人。

sentences.en: I mean, I heard so.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我听说确实如此。

sentences.en: So it is easier to find people in those kinds of technologies, because, you know, developers pretty often want to be ahead of others in terms of technology.
sentences.zh: 所以用这类技术反而更容易招到人，因为你知道，开发者往往希望在技术上走在别人前面。

sentences.en: And companies are more often unwilling to use something that is not yet tested and proven to be working well.
sentences.zh: 而大公司通常更不愿意使用那些尚未经过测试和验证、无法证明运行良好的东西。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So Patrick and I are taking notes here.
sentences.zh: 所以帕特里克和我正在这里记笔记。

sentences.en: If one of these days we ever start a company, we'll make everyone write in Piet or that language that's all brackets or something.
sentences.zh: 如果有一天我们开公司了，我们要让每个人都用Piet或者那种全都是括号的语言来写代码。

sentences.en: I'm just kidding.
sentences.zh: 我开玩笑的。

sentences.en: But that's amazing.
sentences.zh: 但这太厉害了。

sentences.en: I mean, the other thing, too, is it's a way for you to invest in your future.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，另一件重要的事情是，这也是你对未来进行投资的一种方式。

sentences.en: So, you know, if you go to, let's say, maybe a bigger company and they're doing PHP, just like everyone else is doing PHP and you learn PHP, that's great.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，如果你去了一家大公司，假设他们在做PHP，就像其他人都在做PHP一样，你学会了PHP，那挺好的。

sentences.en: But if you can join a company that's, especially if you believe,
sentences.zh: 但如果你能加入一家公司，尤其是当你坚信……

sentences.en: like if you have a crystal ball and you know this language is going to be really big and you join a company that's using it early on, you're kind of investing in your future self.
sentences.zh: 就像如果你拥有一个水晶球，你知道这门语言将来会变得非常火爆，并且你在早期就加入了一家使用它的公司，你其实是在为未来的自己投资。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I've always seen it as a bets we make, you know, they're like those waves that you can go with.
sentences.zh: 我一直把这看作是我们下注的行为，你知道，它们就像你可以顺势而为的浪潮。

sentences.en: If there are those old and lazy waves like Java or Python that I really like and respect, but it is also not pushing you much, you know,
sentences.zh: 如果那是那些陈旧而安逸的浪潮，比如Java或Python——我真的很喜欢也很尊重它们，但它们也不会给你带来太多推力，你知道的，

sentences.en: because there are already plenty of people who know those languages, who have experience, who are teaching it, who have materials, et cetera, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 因为已经有大把的人懂这些语言、有经验、在教这些语言、有现成的资料等等等等。

sentences.en: So it's a very safe way to choose a big language like this one, but it's not something that will by itself push your career.
sentences.zh: 所以选择像这样的大型语言是非常稳妥的方式，但它本身并不会推动你的职业生涯向前发展。

sentences.en: But choosing something that is new and risky is, you know, on one side, it's very risky because this technology might die, literally.
sentences.zh: 而选择那些崭新且充满风险的技术，一方面，它风险极高，因为这项技术可能会消亡，字面意义上的消亡。

sentences.en: But if it goes far, it can push you together with it.
sentences.zh: 但如果它走得远，它就能带着你一起腾飞。

sentences.en: By the way, another thing that I truly believed back then, I remember one thing was Kotlin that really inspired me, that I was really fascinated about.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，我当时深信不疑的另一件事，我记得有一件事是Kotlin真的激励了我，让我深深着迷。

sentences.en: But the second thing I was really passionate about was this multi-platform library called RoboVM.
sentences.zh: 但我同样充满热情的第二件事是一个叫做RoboVM的多平台库。

sentences.en: It does not exist anymore.
sentences.zh: 它现在已经不存在了。

sentences.en: It was a really nice idea that you can write a code in Java or Kotlin that were supported.
sentences.zh: 那是一个非常棒的想法，你可以用当时受支持的Java或Kotlin编写代码。

sentences.en: And this code worked natively on Android, but it also was compiled into a native code on iOS.
sentences.zh: 这些代码不仅能在Android上原生运行，还能被编译成iOS上的原生代码。

sentences.en: And so you could also make a multi-platform applications.
sentences.zh: 所以你也可以开发多平台应用。

sentences.en: So what happened to that?
sentences.zh: 那后来怎么了？

sentences.en: I believe that Microsoft just bought it and killed the project.
sentences.zh: 我猜微软把它买下来然后把这个项目给毙了。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, that happens.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的，这种事时有发生。

sentences.en: And, yeah, and so all the people who invested their time and energy into this fascinating project, you know, lost it.
sentences.zh: 对，所以所有把时间和精力投入到这个迷人项目中的人，你知道的，都白费了。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, that almost happened to Java.
sentences.zh: 我是说，Java也差点遭遇这种命运。

sentences.en: You know, I mean, when Oracle acquired Sun,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，当甲骨文收购Sun时，

sentences.en: there was a period of time where people were uncertain about the legality of using Java and writing your own version of the JVM and all of that.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间人们对使用Java以及编写自己的JVM版本等行为的合法性感到迷茫。

sentences.en: And at that time, people were wondering if Java was really going to survive this legal battle.
sentences.zh: 而在那个时候，人们都在怀疑Java是否真的能挺过这场法律诉讼。

sentences.en: And I think it was just it's just at that state where it's too big to fail or too big to fall or what have you.
sentences.zh: 我想它当时只是达到了那种“大到不能倒”或者“大到不会垮”之类的状态吧。

sentences.en: But but I've seen a lot of, you know, JVM languages, Scala, Kotlin.
sentences.zh: 但我见过很多JVM语言，比如Scala、Kotlin。

sentences.en: There's another one that's I'm totally drawing a blank on.
sentences.zh: 还有另一个，我一时完全想不起来名字了。

sentences.en: There is based on on scheme.
sentences.zh: 有个基于Scheme语言的。

sentences.en: But there's a bunch of these that, you know, run on the JVM, but are slowly kind of eating away at Java.
sentences.zh: 但有这么一群语言，你知道的，它们运行在JVM上，但正在慢慢蚕食Java的市场份额。

sentences.en: And my guess is Java is stable or on the decline.
sentences.zh: 我的猜测是Java目前处于稳定期或者在走下坡路。

sentences.en: But I'd have to look to actually see the data on that.
sentences.zh: 但我得去查查相关数据才能确认。

sentences.en: Yeah, all the data indicate that.
sentences.zh: 是的，所有数据都表明了这一点。

sentences.en: Ah, OK.
sentences.zh: 啊，好的。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There you go.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: So, yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的。

sentences.en: So the type safety and what I noticed when I so I wrote a my own version of Google Photos.
sentences.zh: 类型安全性，还有我注意到的一件事，当时我写了我自己版本的Google相册。

sentences.en: So basically, I have a S3 bucket and whenever I take a photo, my phone waits for Wi-Fi.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，我有一个S3存储桶，每当我拍一张照片，我的手机就会等待Wi-Fi连接。

sentences.en: When it gets Wi-Fi, it looks at all the photos that it doesn't already have on that bucket and it uploads them.
sentences.zh: 一旦连上Wi-Fi，它就会检查该存储桶里还没有哪些照片，然后把它们上传上去。

sentences.en: And so I have just a simple Google Photos clone type thing.
sentences.zh: 所以我只是做了一个简单的Google相册克隆版类似的东西。

sentences.en: And when I wrote it in Kotlin, there's a few things that really stood out to me.
sentences.zh: 当我用Kotlin编写它时，有几件事真的让我印象深刻。

sentences.en: I mean, one was it was literally a decade since I made an Android app.
sentences.zh: 我是说，首先，我距离上次开发Android应用已经过去整整十年了。

sentences.en: So the whole ecosystem is way, way better now than it was 10 years ago.
sentences.zh: 所以整个生态系统现在比10年前好太多了。

sentences.en: But it felt like, you know, I really enjoyed the editor, the integrated experience and all of the sort of quick fixes that were happening.
sentences.zh: 但感觉就是，我很享受这个编辑器、集成开发体验，以及所有那些不断出现的快速修复功能。

sentences.en: And even the fact that I could.
sentences.zh: 甚至包括我能够……

sentences.en: One thing that really shocked me was I could actually take Java code from Stack Overflow or Java files from other projects.
sentences.zh: 真正让我震惊的一点是，我居然可以直接把Stack Overflow上的Java代码或其他项目中的Java文件拿过来。

sentences.en: And I could convert them to Kotlin and it gave it even in line convert blocks of Java code to Kotlin.
sentences.zh: 然后我可以把它们转换成Kotlin，它甚至支持内联转换成块状的Kotlin代码。

sentences.en: That really struck me.
sentences.zh: 这真的触动了我。

sentences.en: It's just amazing how that because it's not trivial to do that.
sentences.zh: 能做到这一点真的很神奇，因为这并非易事。

sentences.en: I found that really pleasant, really surprising.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这非常令人愉快，也非常惊艳。

sentences.en: Yes, that's from the beginning.
sentences.zh: 是的，从一开始就是这样。

sentences.en: Also, you can pretty easily migrate the whole project and that works.
sentences.zh: 而且你可以非常轻松地迁移整个项目，而且确实能行。

sentences.en: However, of course, it's far, far from being a good Kotlin code because it's a Javish code.
sentences.zh: 不过，当然，它离写出优秀的Kotlin代码还差得很远，因为它写出来的还是“Java风格”的代码。

sentences.en: And the next step is to start using Kotlin idioms to improve readability and safety of this solution.
sentences.zh: 而下一步就是开始使用Kotlin的惯用法来提高这个解决方案的可读性和安全性。

sentences.en: You know, but yes, a simple solution can be can be done by this auto transformation.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，不过是的，通过这种自动转换就能实现一个简单的解决方案。

sentences.en: And it works.
sentences.zh: 而且它能用。

sentences.en: It works really nice.
sentences.zh: 它的运行效果真的很棒。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, it's a great way to kind of get started.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这是个很好的起步方式。

sentences.en: And as you said, you can see what's going on there and then rewrite it or update it.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，你可以先看看那里是怎么运作的，然后再重写或更新它。

sentences.en: Yeah, there is actually a cool tool that many beginners use.
sentences.zh: 对，其实有个很多初学者都在用的炫酷工具。

sentences.en: So if you have Android Studio or IntelliJ open, you can just go into tools, Kotlin, show Kotlin bytecode.
sentences.zh: 如果你打开了Android Studio或IntelliJ，你只需进入“Tools -> Kotlin -> Show Kotlin Bytecode”（工具 -> Kotlin -> 显示Kotlin字节码）。

sentences.en: And you can see what your Kotlin code is compiled to.
sentences.zh: 你就能看到你的Kotlin代码被编译成了什么样。

sentences.en: So if you are a fan of JVM bytecode, you can read it there.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你是JVM字节码的粉丝，你可以在那里阅读它。

sentences.en: If you are not, there is this button decompile.
sentences.zh: 如果你不是，还有一个“反编译”（Decompile）按钮。

sentences.en: And this button decompiles your bytecode into Java.
sentences.zh: 这个按钮会将你的字节码反编译成 Java 代码。

sentences.en: It's a strange journey because we compiled Kotlin into JVM bytecode, then they compiled it into Java.
sentences.zh: 这是一个奇妙的过程，因为我们把 Kotlin 编译成 JVM 字节码，然后他们又将其编译成 Java。

sentences.en: And you can see how it works.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到它是如何工作的。

sentences.en: That's a very useful tool for those who come from Java.
sentences.zh: 对于那些熟悉 Java 的人来说，这是一个非常实用的工具。

sentences.en: They are learning Kotlin and they are trying to understand how something works.
sentences.zh: 他们正在学习 Kotlin，并试图理解某些机制是如何运作的。

sentences.en: You can just see how this code would look like if it were written in Java, any code.
sentences.zh: 你可以直接看看这段代码如果用 Java 编写会是什么样子，任何代码都可以。

sentences.en: Yeah, that is super, super cool.
sentences.zh: 是的，这真的超级超级酷。

sentences.en: If I remember correctly, or maybe I'm wrong about this now, but at the time, Java doesn't have coroutines, right?
sentences.zh: 如果我没记错的话，或者可能我现在记错了，但在当时，Java 是没有协程的，对吧？

sentences.en: So if you write coroutines in Kotlin, how does that end up?
sentences.zh: 所以如果你在 Kotlin 中编写协程，最终会变成什么样？

sentences.en: And you try to decompile it.
sentences.zh: 然后你尝试去反编译它。

sentences.en: Do you get an error or what actually happens there?
sentences.zh: 你会得到一个错误，还是实际上会发生什么？

sentences.en: Okay, so maybe I will start with what are coroutines.
sentences.zh: 好的，那也许我先从什么是协程开始讲起。

sentences.en: Yeah, okay.
sentences.zh: 行，好的。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's true.
sentences.zh: 对，确实如此。

sentences.en: It's a good point.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的观点。

sentences.en: So people often say that coroutines are like lightweight threads.
sentences.zh: 所以人们经常说协程就像是轻量级线程。

sentences.en: I think that's, I mean, it can be a good start as it might be a useful metaphor to understand that they are lightweight.
sentences.zh: 我认为这，我的意思是，这可以是一个好的开端，因为它可能是一个有用的隐喻，能帮助理解它们很轻量。

sentences.en: And they are kind of like threads, but it's also very confusing because coroutines are not threads.
sentences.zh: 它们有点像线程，但这也非常容易让人混淆，因为协程并不是线程。

sentences.en: So coroutines are already present in many languages in some limited form.
sentences.zh: 因此，许多语言中其实都已经以某种受限的形式存在协程了。

sentences.en: Coroutines are present in JavaScript, in Python, in C Sharp.
sentences.zh: JavaScript、Python 和 C# 中都有协程。

sentences.en: Any async await block is a coroutine.
sentences.zh: 任何 async/await 块都是一个协程。

sentences.en: Any generator is a coroutine.
sentences.zh: 任何生成器都是一个协程。

sentences.en: But, you know, a very limited use of a coroutine.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，这只是协程非常受限的一种用法。

sentences.en: So now what a coroutine is.
sentences.zh: 那么现在来看看协程到底是什么。

sentences.en: Coroutine is a piece of code, some kind of block that can be suspended at any point.
sentences.zh: 协程是一段代码，某种可以在任何时间点被挂起的代码块。

sentences.en: You know, later you can resume it from that point.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，稍后你可以从那个点恢复它。

sentences.en: So the word suspended is very important because it's not blocked.
sentences.zh: 所以“挂起”这个词非常重要，因为它没有被阻塞。

sentences.en: It is suspended.
sentences.zh: 它是被挂起了。

sentences.en: So it means that when you suspend a coroutine, what you have is a continuation object.
sentences.zh: 这意味着当你挂起一个协程时，你得到的是一个延续对象（continuation object）。

sentences.en: This is an object, an object that has all the local state, literally something like call stack.
sentences.zh: 这是一个对象，一个包含了所有局部状态的对象，字面意思就像是调用栈一样。

sentences.en: So all the local variables of this function, of the function that called it, of the function that called it, et cetera, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 所以这个函数的所有局部变量，调用它的函数的所有局部变量，再上一层调用函数的局部变量，等等，等等。

sentences.en: And so that's what continuation has.
sentences.zh: 这就是延续对象所拥有的内容。

sentences.en: And this object is like a save.
sentences.zh: 这个对象就像是一个存档。

sentences.en: You can keep it in your local memory.
sentences.zh: 你可以把它保存在本地内存中。

sentences.en: Formally, you can even serialize it and later deserialize it.
sentences.zh: 形式上，你甚至可以序列化它，然后在之后反序列化它。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, at any point, you can resume it and continue from where your function stopped.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，在任何时候，你都可以恢复它，并从你的函数停止的地方继续执行。

sentences.en: So it means that you can literally jump in the middle of the function and, you know, start from there.
sentences.zh: 这意味着你可以直接跳入函数的正中间，然后，你知道的，从那里开始。

sentences.en: Perfect implementation of coroutines requires a control of platform to, you know, capture this stack and restore it.
sentences.zh: 协程的完美实现需要对平台进行控制，以便，你知道的，捕获这个栈并恢复它。

sentences.en: Kotlin does not have it because it does not control the platform.
sentences.zh: Kotlin 没有这样做，因为它不控制底层平台。

sentences.en: So it simulates it by having those continuation objects that store it.
sentences.zh: 所以它是通过拥有那些存储了这些状态的延续对象来模拟这一点的。

sentences.en: Wait, hang on.
sentences.zh: 等等，稍等一下。

sentences.en: Let me dive into that because that blows my mind.
sentences.zh: 让我深入了解一下，因为这让我大开眼界。

sentences.en: So how does Kotlin able to store all the local variables?
sentences.zh: 那么 Kotlin 是如何做到存储所有局部变量的呢？

sentences.en: Is that part of the Java JDK where you can get all of that?
sentences.zh: 这是 Java JDK 的一部分吗，你可以通过它获取所有这些？

sentences.en: It's a simpler concept.
sentences.zh: 这是一个更简单的概念。

sentences.en: So in Kotlin, the functions that can be suspended are suspending functions.
sentences.zh: 在 Kotlin 中，可以被挂起的函数被称为挂起函数（suspending functions）。

sentences.en: They have suspend keyword.
sentences.zh: 它们带有 suspend 关键字。

sentences.en: Such a functions under the hood are passing this continuation object that is, you know, a reference to their local state.
sentences.zh: 这样的函数在底层会传递这个延续对象，也就是，你知道的，指向它们局部状态的引用。

sentences.en: And this object is used to keep this local state when someone suspends it.
sentences.zh: 当有人将其挂起时，就会使用这个对象来保存这个局部状态。

sentences.en: So the very important thing to notice is that this is not an additional cost because, I mean, it is, but a very small one because we are not copying this state.
sentences.zh: 所以需要注意非常重要的一点是，这不会产生额外的开销——我的意思是，确实有一点，但非常小，因为我们没有复制这个状态。

sentences.en: We are only adding another reference to it.
sentences.zh: 我们只是为它添加了另一个引用。

sentences.en: So if you have a local variable with a list that is placed somewhere in the memory, you know, the variable is a reference to a point in a memory, okay?
sentences.zh: 所以如果你有一个局部变量，里面有一个列表，它被放在内存中的某个地方，你知道的，这个变量是指向内存中某个点的引用，对吧？

sentences.en: Then the continuation does not have a liSt.
sentences.zh: 然后延续对象并没有持有一个列表。

sentences.en: It has a reference to the same point in the memory.
sentences.zh: 它持有的是指向内存中同一个点的引用。

sentences.en: So creating those continuation objects is super cheap because, you know, you're not copying the state.
sentences.zh: 因此，创建这些延续对象的成本超级低，因为，你知道的，你没有复制状态。

sentences.en: It's like a shallow copy.
sentences.zh: 这就像是一个浅拷贝。

sentences.en: Yes, it's like a shallow copy, but we want it this way.
sentences.zh: 是的，这就像是一个浅拷贝，但我们就是希望这样。

sentences.en: Yes, we want it this way because, you know, if the continuation is suspended, then the local variables are gone because, you know, your execution is finished for this coroutine.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们希望这样，因为，你知道的，如果延续被挂起了，那么局部变量就消失了，因为，你知道的，这个协程的执行已经结束了。

sentences.en: But, you know, you still have a single reference to that in the continuation.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，你在延续对象中仍然保留着对它的单一引用。

sentences.en: And that's how it works.
sentences.zh: 这就是它的工作原理。

sentences.en: And that's pretty smart.
sentences.zh: 这真是太聪明了。

sentences.en: Of course, if, because Java has plans to introduce coroutines.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果——因为 Java 有引入协程的计划。

sentences.en: And I believe that they will introduce them in a century or two from now on.
sentences.zh: 我相信他们会在从现在算起的一两个世纪后引入它们。

sentences.en: And Kotlin is designed to support that if they finally introduce that.
sentences.zh: 而 Kotlin 的设计就是为了在他们最终引入时能够支持这一点。

sentences.en: Yeah, that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这很有道理。

sentences.en: One place where I found myself needing to use coroutines, and this goes way back, I wanted to make a, like, an RPG game.
sentences.zh: 我发现自己需要使用协程的一个场景，这要追溯到很久以前，当时我想做一个类似 RPG 的游戏。

sentences.en: And I was, this was a long time ago.
sentences.zh: 而且那是很久以前的事了。

sentences.en: I was actually in high school, I think, and I only knew C++.
sentences.zh: 我当时还在读高中，我想，而且我只懂 C++。

sentences.en: And, you know, if you've ever played any of these RPGs, you go to the town and there's people walking around in the town.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，如果你玩过任何这些 RPG 游戏，你会走到城镇里，镇上有人走来走去。

sentences.en: And you can walk up to them and you can walk up to them and press the button on a joystick or a keyboard or whatever and start a conversation, right?
sentences.zh: 你可以走到他们跟前，你可以走到他们旁边，按下操纵杆或键盘或诸如此类的按钮，然后开始对话，对吧？

sentences.en: And they have some dialogue that they'll say on command.
sentences.zh: 他们会按指令说出一些台词。

sentences.en: When you're not talking to them, they're kind of wandering aimlessly or maybe they have a path that they follow or what have you.
sentences.zh: 当你没和他们说话时，他们就在漫无目的地闲逛，或者可能他们有一条遵循的路径，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And so, you know, each person is kind of, you know, operating on their own timeline.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，每个人都在自己的时间线上运行。

sentences.en: Like, you don't want every person in the town to move at exactly the same time.
sentences.zh: 比如，你不会希望镇上的每个人都在完全相同的时间移动。

sentences.en: It would look very robotic and weird, right?
sentences.zh: 那看起来会非常机械和诡异，对吧？

sentences.en: So you want to have each person sort of with their own timer that says, okay, you know, a few seconds have passed.
sentences.zh: 所以你希望每个人都有他们自己的计时器，显示着，好吧，你知道的，几秒钟过去了。

sentences.en: Let's move to the bookshelf and let's take some steps.
sentences.zh: 让我们移动到书架旁，走几步。

sentences.en: Or, you know, I just took a step.
sentences.zh: 或者，你知道的，我刚迈出一步。

sentences.en: Now I have to wait a second.
sentences.zh: 现在我必须等待一秒钟。

sentences.en: And so, you know, again, this is very early.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，再次强调，这非常早期。

sentences.en: So I thought, oh, I'll just have each person become their own thread.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，哦，我只要让每个人都变成他们自己的线程就行了。

sentences.en: And when they're not walking, the thread will just be sleeping.
sentences.zh: 当他们不走路时，线程就会进入睡眠状态。

sentences.en: And what I found is, yeah, you actually can't create thousands and thousands and thousands of literal threads because there's so much overhead there.
sentences.zh: 而我发现的是，是的，你实际上无法创建成千上万个真正的线程，因为那里的开销太大了。

sentences.en: And even a thread that's asleep, you know, consumes a lot of resources.
sentences.zh: 即使是一个处于睡眠状态的线程，你知道的，也会消耗大量的资源。

sentences.en: And it turns out if you have a ton of threads that are asleep, you end up running out of cores and it's just kind of a mess, right?
sentences.zh: 结果证明，如果你有大量的线程在睡眠，你最终会耗尽 CPU 核心，这简直是一团糟，对吧？

sentences.en: So you end up having to do something else or you kind of like visit all of these characters and wake them up and say, hey, are you ready to do anything?
sentences.zh: 所以你最终不得不做别的事情，或者你得去访问所有这些角色并唤醒他们，说：嘿，你们准备好做什么了吗？

sentences.en: And they say, oh, no, I need to sleep for another, you know, cycle.
sentences.zh: 然后他们说，哦，不，我需要再睡一个，你知道的，周期。

sentences.en: I'll walk next cycle.
sentences.zh: 我会在下一个周期走路。

sentences.en: And so you go to the next one.
sentences.zh: 于是你再去访问下一个。

sentences.en: So every cycle, you kind of round robin, go through all these villagers, you know, kind of waking them up, letting them do a cycle and then going to the next one.
sentences.zh: 所以每个周期，你都要轮询（round robin）遍历所有这些村民，你知道的，把他们唤醒，让他们运行一个周期，然后转到下一个。

sentences.en: So if you're in an internal state, it needs to, like, wait, you know, 27 cycles before taking the next step, you have to go and update that internal state.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你处于某种内部状态，需要像这样等待，你知道的，27 个周期才能迈出下一步，你就必须去更新那个内部状态。

sentences.en: And everything now has to be in, like, you know, C++ has to be in, like, a dictionary or something.
sentences.zh: 现在所有东西都必须放在，比如，你知道的，在 C++ 中必须放在字典（dictionary）之类的东西里。

sentences.en: And so you lose type safety and it feels very unnatural, right?
sentences.zh: 这样一来你就失去了类型安全，而且感觉非常不自然，对吧？

sentences.en: What's better is if you could actually have, like, you know, not literally a process, like a Unix process, but have, like, a, you know, separate routine for each, you know,
sentences.zh: 更好的做法是，如果你能实际拥有，比如，你知道的，不是真正的进程，就像 Unix 进程那样，而是为每个，你知道的，

sentences.en: villager.
sentences.zh: 村民拥有一个独立的例程（routine）。

sentences.en: And in that routine, you could say, you know, sleep for a second and take a step and do this forever and not have to worry about all the overhead and let the OS handle, you know,
sentences.zh: 在这个例程中，你可以说，你知道的，睡眠一秒钟，然后迈出一步，永远这样重复下去，而不必担心所有的开销，并让操作系统去处理，你知道的，

sentences.en: keeping the state of all those people and everything.
sentences.zh: 维护所有这些人以及一切的状态。

sentences.en: And so, you know, at the time, I didn't know about coroutines, so, you know, I had to implement a really ugly way.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，当时我并不知道协程，所以，你知道的，我不得不实现一种非常丑陋的方法。

sentences.en: But I've always found coroutines is a really elegant, kind of beautiful way of handling, you know, many,
sentences.zh: 但我一直觉得协程是一种真正优雅、美丽的途径，用来处理，你知道的，许多，

sentences.en: many objects that all need to have their own internal state at the same time.
sentences.zh: 许多都需要同时拥有各自内部状态的对象。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: But I will probably synchronize it with a single timer anyway.
sentences.zh: 但我无论如何可能还是会用一个单一的计时器来同步它。

sentences.en: Anyway, I haven't done a big game project, but in a small one, I wouldn't like having independent timers for different parts of a game because, you know,
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，我没有做过大型游戏项目，但在一个小项目中，我不会喜欢让游戏的各个部分拥有独立的计时器，因为，你知道的，

sentences.en: then your game is overloading your computer.
sentences.zh: 那样你的游戏就会使电脑超负荷。

sentences.en: Some things are getting slow and now all the elements are, you know, living in their own time.
sentences.zh: 有些事情变慢了，现在所有的元素都在，你知道的，按照它们自己的时间运转。

sentences.en: I generally believe there is a tendency to rather synchronize everything with a single clock, and I would rather use objects.
sentences.zh: 我深信有一种倾向，宁愿用单一的时钟同步一切，我更愿意使用对象。

sentences.en: However, you could, the actor model seems like something that could be helpful in here.
sentences.zh: 不过，你可以这样做，演员模型（actor model）似乎在这里能派上用场。

sentences.en: And in Kotlin, we use coroutines for the actor model.
sentences.zh: 在 Kotlin 中，我们使用协程来实现演员模型。

sentences.en: Yeah, why don't you dive into that?
sentences.zh: 是的，你为什么不详细讲讲这个呢？

sentences.en: So, like, there's a lot of folks here who have maybe never built an app.
sentences.zh: 所以，这里有很多人可能从来没有开发过应用。

sentences.en: They do web or they do backend or something like that.
sentences.zh: 他们做网页前端、后端或者诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: So, kind of connect us from sort of the app development to coroutines.
sentences.zh: 所以，请把我们从应用开发过渡到协程上来讲讲。

sentences.en: When are they used?
sentences.zh: 它们什么时候被使用？

sentences.en: What's the, you know, kind of best use for them?
sentences.zh: 它们的，你知道的，最佳用途是什么？

sentences.en: And why are they a good idea?
sentences.zh: 为什么它们是一个好主意？

sentences.en: Okay, so there are a few typical use cases.
sentences.zh: 好的，这里有几个典型的用例。

sentences.en: So, the most typical one is that, let's say that you, on your application, you need to fetch some data from the internet.
sentences.zh: 最典型的一个是，比方说你在应用中需要从互联网获取一些数据。

sentences.en: And you need to wait for those data because it takes some time to get them from your API.
sentences.zh: 你需要等待这些数据，因为从你的 API 获取它们需要一些时间。

sentences.en: And the question is, how do you wait for that?
sentences.zh: 问题是，你如何等待这个过程？

sentences.en: So, if you block your threat while waiting for the response, you need to well-manage threats because there are some threats you should not block.
sentences.zh: 如果你在等待响应时阻塞了线程，你就需要很好地管理线程，因为有些线程是不应该被阻塞的。

sentences.en: Other threats you can block, but they are expensive and you should not block too many of them.
sentences.zh: 其他线程你可以阻塞，但它们开销很大，你不应该阻塞太多。

sentences.en: So, that's problematic.
sentences.zh: 所以，这很有问题。

sentences.en: So, coroutines solve that problem.
sentences.zh: 因此，协程解决了这个问题。

sentences.en: You just suspend the coroutine when you wait for something and resume it when you got it.
sentences.zh: 你在等待某些东西时只需挂起协程，获取到之后再恢复它。

sentences.en: Then, using coroutines, it's pretty easy to implement async await.
sentences.zh: 然后，使用协程可以非常轻松地实现 async/await。

sentences.en: I mean, they are built into the Kotlin coroutines library.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它们是内置在 Kotlin 协程库中的。

sentences.en: And there are two parts of Kotlin coroutines.
sentences.zh: Kotlin 协程包含两个部分。

sentences.en: There is a built-in support that, you know, gives you the capability to suspend, start coroutine, etc.
sentences.zh: 一部分是内置支持，你知道的，它赋予你挂起、启动协程等能力。

sentences.en: There is a library that gives you tools like async await or sequence generators, etc., etc.
sentences.zh: 另一部分是一个库，它为你提供诸如 async/await 或序列生成器等工具。

sentences.en: And with yield.
sentences.zh: 还有 yield。

sentences.en: And so, then, pretty often we use async await in a similar way as in other languages, but, you know, they are implemented using coroutines.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们经常会以类似于其他语言的方式使用 async/await，但它们，你知道的，是通过协程实现的。

sentences.en: Another thing is that if you are implementing a backend application, as Jason mentioned in here,
sentences.zh: 另一件事是，如果你正在实现一个后端应用，正如杰森在这里提到的，

sentences.en: if you start too many threats, it's a huge cost for your computer.
sentences.zh: 如果你启动了太多的线程，这对你的计算机来说是一个巨大的开销。

sentences.en: So, if you have a pool of threats that you use on your backend system and you have lots but lots of requests,
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你的后端系统使用了一个线程池，并且有大量大量的请求，

sentences.en: then you need to start a lot of threats on your pool or you need to make your requests wait, what is not optimal.
sentences.zh: 那么你需要在池中启动大量的线程，或者让你的请求排队等待，这并不是最优解。

sentences.en: Each threat is at least one megabyte of data.
sentences.zh: 每个线程至少占用一兆字节的数据。

sentences.en: Each threat allocates one megabyte of data.
sentences.zh: 每个线程分配一兆字节的数据。

sentences.en: It is also a significant cost from the perspective of processor or operating system synchronization.
sentences.zh: 从处理器或操作系统同步的角度来看，这也是一个显著的开销。

sentences.en: So, if you start having, let's say, thousand threats, it's already a visible burden on your processor time, you know, the energy used only to manage them.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你开始拥有，比方说，一千个线程，这已经对你的处理器时间造成了肉眼可见的负担，你知道的，仅仅是用来管理它们的能量消耗。

sentences.en: And it's already one gigabyte of RAM at leaSt.
sentences.zh: 而且内存占用至少已经达到一吉字节（1GB）了。

sentences.en: If you have 10,000 of them, that's very, very unlikely your application will work fine.
sentences.zh: 如果你有一万个线程，你的应用还能正常运行的可能性微乎其微。

sentences.en: And, you know, in a big systems, you know, having those numbers of requests is not so hard to reach.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，在一个大型系统中，达到这样的请求数量并不是很难。

sentences.en: Which, yeah, the other thing is you can really shoot yourself in the foot.
sentences.zh: 而且，另一件事是，你真的会搬起石头砸自己的脚。

sentences.en: I have a couple of stories.
sentences.zh: 我有一两个故事。

sentences.en: One, Patrick and I worked together a really long time ago.
sentences.zh: 一个是我和帕特里克（Patrick）在很久很久以前一起工作过。

sentences.en: And we worked on a project where we were doing some image processing.
sentences.zh: 我们当时在一个项目中做一些图像处理工作。

sentences.en: And we were trying, you know, kind of a new way of doing image processing.
sentences.zh: 我们当时正在尝试，你知道的，一种做图像处理的新方法。

sentences.en: And basically, this was all, we were prototyping something on the desktop.
sentences.zh: 基本上，这一切都是我们在桌面上做原型开发。

sentences.en: And I'm pretty sure, you can correct me on this, Patrick, but I'm pretty sure what we did was we created a new, either a new thread or a new process for every frame.
sentences.zh: 我很确定——帕特里克你可以纠正我，但我非常确定我们当时做的是，我们为每一帧创建了一个新的线程或者一个新的进程。

sentences.en: And, you know, again, this is, you know, us not knowing what we're doing.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，这又是我们不知道自己在做什么的情况。

sentences.en: And so we couldn't figure out why, you know, right around like 20,000, 30,000 frames, the Python program died.
sentences.zh: 所以我们搞不懂为什么，你知道的，差不多在大约2万到3万帧的时候，Python程序就崩溃了。

sentences.en: And then we would have to, like, run it again on the next 30,000 frames.
sentences.zh: 然后我们不得不，比如说，在接下来的3万帧上再次运行它。

sentences.en: And it's because, you know, we didn't really know what we were doing.
sentences.zh: 这是因为，你知道的，我们其实不知道自己在做什么。

sentences.en: We didn't realize, okay, there's this huge overhead.
sentences.zh: 我们没有意识到，好吧，这里有这么大的开销。

sentences.en: And if I, you know, if I, what I really need to do is use a thread pool or even better, use async await, which has a thread pool under the hood and takes care of that for you.
sentences.zh: 如果我，你知道的，如果我，我真正需要做的是使用线程池，或者更好的是，使用 async await，它底层自带线程池并为你处理好这一切。

sentences.en: A similar story, there was actually a period of time where, you know, the street view,
sentences.zh: 一个类似的故事，其实有一段时间，你知道的，街景服务，

sentences.en: which is the Google Maps where you can go down to the street level and see the photos of the street, that service actually leaked threads.
sentences.zh: 也就是你可以下到街道级别并查看街道照片的谷歌地图，那个服务实际上会泄漏线程。

sentences.en: So there was some part of that service that was creating threads and not releasing them, like not cleaning them up.
sentences.zh: 所以该服务的一部分在创建线程却没有释放它们，比如没有清理它们。

sentences.en: And so there's a period of time, and when I say period of time, I'm talking years,
sentences.zh: 因此有一段时间，当我说一段时间时，我指的是几年，

sentences.en: where the street view service, you know, a single instance of that service could only live for a few hours
sentences.zh: 街景服务，你知道的，该服务的一个实例只能存活几个小时，

sentences.en: because it would eventually allocate too many threads and get killed by the hypervisor.
sentences.zh: 因为它最终会分配太多线程并被系统管理程序杀死。

sentences.en: And so the solution for maybe not years, but definitely for about half a year, the solution was to just, you know, keep enough services, enough instances up and running.
sentences.zh: 所以解决方案——也许不是几年，但绝对有大约半年时间，解决方案就是，你知道的，保持足够的服务、足够的实例处于启动和运行状态。

sentences.en: And so for like half a year, street view limped along with that.
sentences.zh: 所以在大概半年的时间里，街景服务就是靠着这种方式勉强维持的。

sentences.en: And, you know, async await solves all of that.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，async await 解决了所有这些问题。

sentences.en: I mean, you still have to do tuning and all of that if you're performance conscious, but it's very hard, much harder to shoot yourself in the foot with async await.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你注重性能，你仍然需要进行调优之类的，但使用 async await 要想搬起石头砸自己的脚是非常困难的，难得多。

sentences.en: So in Kotlin, we use coroutines.
sentences.zh: 所以在 Kotlin 中，我们使用协程。

sentences.en: We use coroutines.
sentences.zh: 我们使用协程。

sentences.en: We start a requeSt.
sentences.zh: 我们发起一个请求。

sentences.en: The typical approach right now is to handle each request in a separate coroutine.
sentences.zh: 目前典型的做法是在单独的协程中处理每个请求。

sentences.en: And those coroutines have their own pool of threads because the Kotlin coroutines library has a default built-in support for pool of threads
sentences.zh: 这些协程拥有它们自己的线程池，因为 Kotlin 协程库对线程池具有默认的内置支持，

sentences.en: so that when you start a coroutine, you can decide on what pool of threads it is supposed to run.
sentences.zh: 以便当你启动一个协程时，你可以决定它应该在哪个线程池上运行。

sentences.en: And if in this case, it will run on the optimal number of threads for your machine.
sentences.zh: 如果在这个情况下，它将在适合你机器的最佳线程数上运行。

sentences.en: And that is, of course, the number of cores on your machine.
sentences.zh: 这当然就是你机器上的核心数。

sentences.en: So if you have a 16 core server, it will start 16 cores and probably tens of thousands of requests will, you know, be on tens of thousands of coroutines.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你有一个 16 核的服务器，它会启动 16 个核心，可能成千上万个请求会，你知道的，在成千上万个协程上运行。

sentences.en: That is practically no burden at all that are running on those 16 threads interchangeably
sentences.zh: 这实际上完全没有负担，它们在这 16 个线程上交替运行，

sentences.en: only when they are needed, whenever they are waiting for something like response from database or from another service, the coroutines are suspended.
sentences.zh: 仅在需要时运行，每当它们等待诸如来自数据库或另一个服务的响应之类的东西时，协程就会被挂起。

sentences.en: But suspending and restreaming is a very cheap operation.
sentences.zh: 但挂起和重新调度是一个非常廉价的操作。

sentences.en: So it's very, very close to the optimal.
sentences.zh: 所以它非常非常接近最优状态。

sentences.en: That is, you know, the theoretical way where, you know, processor only does what it should do.
sentences.zh: 也就是，你知道的，处理器只做它应该做的事情的理论方式。

sentences.en: So business logic of yours.
sentences.zh: 也就是你的业务逻辑。

sentences.en: Yeah, one thing I always wondered, and I never took the time to do an experiment to find this out, you probably know this offhand, is, you know, let's say you have 16 cores
sentences.zh: 对，我一直想知道的一件事——我从来没有花时间去做实验来弄清楚这一点，你可能对此外行也很清楚，就是，你知道的，假设你有 16 个核心，

sentences.en: and I create 17 coroutines and they all have a lot of work to do.
sentences.zh: 我创建了 17 个协程，它们都有大量的工作要做。

sentences.en: Does it share time between those 17 or does it finish the first 16 and then do the 17?
sentences.zh: 它是在这 17 个协程之间分摊时间，还是先完成前 16 个然后才做第 17 个？

sentences.en: So coroutines can only switch at the suspension points.
sentences.zh: 所以协程只能在挂起点进行切换。

sentences.en: So if those coroutines never suspend, what is very unlikely, because we generally use coroutines to do things that are suspending.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果这些协程从不挂起——这极不可能，因为我们通常使用协程来做需要挂起的事情，

sentences.en: So if they never suspend the, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以如果它们从不挂起，你知道的，

sentences.en: you said 16 and 17, so 16 of them will work, you know, until the first of them is done and then the 17th will be able to start.
sentences.zh: 你说了 16 和 17，所以其中 16 个会工作，你知道的，直到它们当中的第一个完成，然后第 17 个才能开始。

sentences.en: However, even in such extremely rare situations, there are good practices, like using there is this yield function with no arguments that is only a suspension point,
sentences.zh: 然而，即使在如此极端罕见的情况下，也有很好的做法，比如使用这个没有参数的 yield 函数，它仅仅是一个挂起点，

sentences.en: only a place where you can have a switch and give another coroutines a time for processing.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是一个你可以进行切换并给其他协程处理时间的地方。

sentences.en: I use it extremely, extremely rarely, probably only a few times in my life, because it only makes sense in processes that are, you know,
sentences.zh: 我极少极少使用它，可能我一生中只用过几次，因为它只在以下进程中有意义：

sentences.en: either that are blocking threads without suspension for a very, very long time.
sentences.zh: 要么是在没有挂起的情况下长时间阻塞线程的进程。

sentences.en: So either doing a lot of work or doing a lot of, or doing some waiting.
sentences.zh: 所以要么是在做大量的工作，要么是在做大量的，或者在做一些等待。

sentences.en: But in such a case, there is also a different case, because if you have a coroutine that is waiting, you are not using the pool of threads that is designed to be efficient,
sentences.zh: 但在这种情况下，也有另一种情况，因为如果你有一个正在等待的协程，你使用的就不是旨在高效的线程池，

sentences.en: but instead a different one that is called dispatchers.io that is designed to be blocked.
sentences.zh: 而是另一个专为阻塞而设计的名为 dispatchers.io 的线程池。

sentences.en: So there are, as I said, there are different pool of threads for different purposes.
sentences.zh: 所以正如我所说，针对不同的目的有不同的线程池。

sentences.en: If you have things that are blocking, there is a dispatchers.io to be blocked.
sentences.zh: 如果你有会被阻塞的事情，就有 dispatchers.io 来负责阻塞。

sentences.en: If you have things that are, that should be CPU intensive, that are, that are doing, you know, processing, there is dispatchers default that has as many coroutines,
sentences.zh: 如果你有应该占用 CPU 密集型、正在做，你知道的，处理的事情，就有 dispatchers default，它拥有的协程数量，

sentences.en: as many threads as you have cores on your CPU.
sentences.zh: 和你的 CPU 核心数一样多。

sentences.en: And on Android, the most popular is dispatchers main, that is a pool of threads that only has one thread that is the main thread, that is the most important thread on Android.
sentences.zh: 而在 Android 上，最受欢迎的是 dispatchers main，这是一个只包含一个线程的线程池，即主线程，它是 Android 上最重要的线程。

sentences.en: So by the way, actually, that's, that's also funny, because people think that coroutines means multiple threads,
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，实际上，这也是，这也是有趣的，因为人们认为协程意味着多个线程，

sentences.en: and it can mean that, but pretty often, that's, that's, that's a lazy development, but never, nevertheless, many, many companies do that.
sentences.zh: 它确实可以意味着那个，但相当经常地，那是，那是，那是懒惰的开发，不过尽管如此，许多许多公司都在这样做。

sentences.en: Pretty often, Android projects run only on a single thread, that is the main thread, and it's perfectly fine, because it's never blocked.
sentences.zh: 相当经常地，Android 项目只在一个线程上运行，也就是主线程，这完全没问题，因为它从不被阻塞。

sentences.en: So, I mean, it's not perfectly fine if you do too much work, but if you, if you are not doing any CPU intensive things,
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，如果你做了太多工作，这就不是完全没问题，但如果你，如果你没有做任何 CPU 密集型的事情，

sentences.en: only, you know, a thin client, you know, fetching data and displaying them, it's generally fine.
sentences.zh: 只有，你知道的，一个轻量客户端，你知道的，获取数据并显示它们，通常是没问题的。

sentences.en: Because with coroutines, you never block the threads, you only, only use it when you, when you need it, when you need to use it.
sentences.zh: 因为有了协程，你从不阻塞线程，你只在，当你需要时，当你需要使用它时才使用它。

sentences.en: And that's, that's a valid approach for a, for simple applications with no CPU intensive operations.
sentences.zh: 对于没有 CPU 密集型操作的简单应用程序来说，这是一种，这是一种有效的方法。

sentences.en: That makes sense.
sentences.zh: 这说得通。

sentences.en: So, so, yeah, totally makes sense.
sentences.zh: 所以，所以，是的，完全说得通。

sentences.en: I think, let's use the photos app example.
sentences.zh: 我想，让我们用相册应用这个例子。

sentences.en: You know, if I, I do a scan using the SQLite, I think it's called Room, the wrapper around SQLite on Android, but, but I have some SQLite query, I compare it to my media,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果我，我使用 SQLite 进行扫描——我想它叫 Room，也就是 Android 上 SQLite 的包装器，但，但如果我有一些 SQLite 查询，我把它跟我的媒体进行对比，

sentences.en: and I'm forgetting all the jargon here, my media service, and it says, okay, I have these 400 images to upload.
sentences.zh: 我这里把所有术语都忘了，我的媒体服务，它说，好吧，我有这 400 张图片要上传。

sentences.en: So I can start 400 coroutines right off the bat.
sentences.zh: 所以我可以直接一下子启动 400 个协程。

sentences.en: It'll only start maybe eight of them at a time.
sentences.zh: 它可能一次只启动其中的大约 8 个。

sentences.en: If I say eight cores, you know, should be already threads should be, you know, allocated for this, wait for those eight to finish and do the next one.
sentences.zh: 如果我说 8 个核心，你知道的，应该已经有线程应该被，你知道的，分配给这个任务，等待那 8 个完成然后做下一个。

sentences.en: But I can start all 10,000 of them because the overhead is, is so low.
sentences.zh: 但我可以启动所有 10,000 个，因为开销是，是如此之低。

sentences.en: And then, you know, and then eventually it'll chew through all of those and finish.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道的，然后最终它会处理完所有这些并完成。

sentences.en: What about, yeah, if something is, is really CPU heavy, like for example,
sentences.zh: 那如果，是的，如果有东西，是真正繁重的 CPU 任务，比如，

sentences.en: I want to detect faces in the photo on the phone for some reason, I don't actually do this, but let's say as, as a thought experiment.
sentences.zh: 出于某种原因我想在手机上的照片中检测人脸，我实际上并没有这样做，但假设作为一个思想实验。

sentences.en: So it sounds like, you know, correct me if I'm, if I'm wrong here.
sentences.zh: 所以听起来，你知道的，如果我，如果我这里说错了请纠正我。

sentences.en: It sounds like what you would do is you would create a thread pool.
sentences.zh: 听起来你会做的是创建一个线程池。

sentences.en: That's maybe not all the cores.
sentences.zh: 那可能不是所有的核心。

sentences.en: Cause you don't want to, you know, maximize someone's phone.
sentences.zh: 因为你不想，你知道的，把某个人的手机榨干。

sentences.en: And then you would put these 10,000 requests into that smaller thread pool.
sentences.zh: 然后你会把这 10,000 个请求放入那个较小的线程池中。

sentences.en: That's not the main pool or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 那不是主线程池或类似的东西。

sentences.en: And then those, those coroutines will, you know,
sentences.zh: 然后那些，那些协程会，你知道的，

sentences.en: monopolize that thread pool until they're all done.
sentences.zh: 垄断那个线程池直到它们全部完成。

sentences.en: But it won't kind of, you know, make your phone burn a hole through your pocket or anything.
sentences.zh: 但它不会那种，你知道的，让你的手机把口袋烧个洞或什么的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: There are, there are tools for that.
sentences.zh: 有，有对应的工具。

sentences.en: You can limit parallelism for a, for, for, for, for, for, for your usage.
sentences.zh: 你可以为，为，为，为，为，为你的使用限制并行性。

sentences.zh: 我书中关于 dispatchers 的整章，

sentences.en: Kotlin Coroutines is, is about that.
